#         "Flight Measurements of Drag and Base Pressure of a Fin-Stabilized
#          Parabolic Body of Revolution (NACA RM-10) at Different Reynolds
#          Numbers and at Mach Numbers from 0.9 to 3.3
column2:
#         NACA Technical Note 3320, November 1954.
#         (Supersedes NACA RM L50G24, 1950.)
#         Authors: Langley Aeronautical Laboratory / Pilotless Aircraft
#          Research Division, Wallops Island.
#         NTRS: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19930084086
#         Local PDF: paper/data/pdf/NACA_TN_3320.pdf
#
# Vehicle: NACA RM-10 research model, parabolic-arc body of revolution,
#          rocket-boosted, telemetered free-flight model.
#   Parabolic body (cut at 81.25% of basic length to allow rocket jet at base)
#   Actual body fineness ratio (length / max diameter) = 12.2
#   Full-scale body length = 12.208 ft (146.5 in, 3.7211 m)
#   Full-scale max diameter = 12.0 in (0.3048 m); base diameter = 7.272 in (0.1847 m)
#   Body profile (full-scale, from Fig. 1, x measured from station of Y_max):
#          Y(in) = 6.000 - 0.0007407 * x^2
#   Four 60-deg sweptback fins at base, untapered planform:
#          Total aspect ratio = 2.04
#          Fin cross-section: 10% t/c circular-arc normal to LE
#                             (= 5% streamwise thickness ratio)
#          Fin LE origin station = 129 in; fins extend to station 146.5 in
#          Tip-to-tip span across fins = 35.88 in (0.9114 m)
#          Per-fin exposed semi-span ≈ 13.07 in (0.332 m)
#
# Test: Free-flight, rocket-boosted models. Deceleration-phase data after
#       burnout. Velocity and total drag from CW Doppler radar and telemetered
#       longitudinal accelerometer. Trajectory / atmospheric data from SCR 584
#       radar and radiosondes.
#       Nine models total (4 full-scale, 5 half-scale).
#       Full-scale:  M 0.85 – 3.30, Re_L = 14e6 – 210e6 (based on body length)
#       Half-scale:  M 0.90 – 3.02, Re_L = 15e6 – 110e6
#       Reported accuracy for mean CDT curves: ~±0.005 supersonic,
#       ~±0.01 transonic/subsonic; individual-shot scatter ±0.008 (full-scale)
#       to ±0.015 (half-scale).
#
# This benchmark is INDEPENDENT of the Basic Finner (ADA636861):
#   - Different vehicle (parabolic body vs cone-cylinder, f.r. 12.2 vs 10.0)
#   - Different fin geometry (60-deg swept circular-arc vs rectangular flat slab)
#   - Different test facility (NACA Langley / Wallops vs DREV Valcartier)
#   - Different decade (1950/1954 vs 1997)
#   - Different test technique (rocket-boosted telemetered free flight +
#     Doppler radar vs aeroballistic range photographic tracking)
#
# Data below:
#   CDT_full_scale  = mean-curve total drag coefficient, full-scale model
#                     (based on max body frontal area 0.785 sq ft)
#   CDT_half_scale  = mean-curve total drag coefficient, half-scale model
#                     (based on max body frontal area 0.196 sq ft)
#   Both are zero-lift (fin-stabilized, alpha ~= 0 deg).
#
# Digitization source: Figures 7 (full-scale, 4 models, Doppler + telemeter),
#                      Figure 8 (half-scale, 5 models), and Figure 10
#                      (averaged-curve comparison). Anchor points explicitly
#                      quoted in text:
#   - Full-scale maximum CDT = 0.26 at M = 1.04
#   - Full-scale CDT = 0.21 at M = 2.5
#   - Full-scale CDT = 0.17 at M = 3.3
#   - Half-scale maximum CDT = 0.25 at M = 1.05
#   - Half-scale CDT = 0.19 at M = 3.0
#   - Both curves converge to CDT = 0.195 at M = 2.9
#
# Where one column is blank (") the Mach number is outside that model's
# tested range (half-scale only goes to M ≈ 3.02, full-scale max is 3.30).
